subject.title: [Bug]: Google Chat: Space/Group messages silently ignored (DMs work correctly)

question: Should Google Chat Space ingress satisfy `requireMention` from delivered @mention webhook events when annotation matching fails, or should OpenClaw keep strict `USER_MENTION`/`botUser` matching and require operators to disable `requireMention` per space?
rationale: The source path and latest release evidence show the remaining drop is in mention activation, but choosing an implicit-mention fallback changes group admission semantics for Google Chat Spaces and needs maintainer intent plus live payload proof.

options.title: Fix Mention Activation With Live Proof
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, capture a redacted current Google Chat Space event, and patch plugin-owned mention activation so real @mentions satisfy `requireMention` without broadening sender or Space access.

options.title: Keep Strict Matching And Document Workaround
options.body: Preserve the current gate, improve diagnostics/docs for `botUser` and per-space `requireMention: false`, and close only after maintainers decide that strict annotation matching is intended behavior.

options.title: Consolidate Into Broader Google Chat Routing
options.body: Move the remaining work to a broader Google Chat routing item only if maintainers want mention detection, thread routing, and all-message Space ingestion handled as one product decision.

recommendation.title: Fix Mention Activation With Live Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, capture a redacted current Google Chat Space event, and patch plugin-owned mention activation so real @mentions satisfy `requireMention` without broadening sender or Space access.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current mention-gating and access-policy boundary is recent work by steipete on Google Chat monitor/access and shared inbound mention policy.
